hero.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes as negotiations continue
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have escalated military hostilities during an ongoing ceasefire, with each side conducting strikes and accusing the other of violations. The exchange threatens to derail peace negotiations aimed at ending the three-month conflict.

U.S. Central Command forces shot down four Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz and struck a ground control station in Iran's Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. American officials described the actions as "measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire."

Within two hours, Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded by targeting an American base in Kuwait, claiming it was the source of the U.S. strikes. Kuwait's military confirmed it intercepted hostile missile and drone threats early Thursday morning. Iran also reported that its forces fired at four vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz without coordination with security forces.

The tit-for-tat strikes underscored the fragility of the ceasefire announced in April and exposed the significant distance between the two nations in peace talks. President Trump said he faces no pressure to rush a deal with Iran, stating that Tehran wants to make an agreement but "hasn't gotten there." He claimed Iran was "negotiating on fumes" and refused to accelerate the diplomatic timeline in response to renewed fighting.

At a White House cabinet meeting, Trump also directed warnings at regional players, saying the Strait of Hormuz would remain "open to everybody" and threatening consequences for Oman if it did not comply with U.S. expectations regarding control of the waterway. The White House called Iranian claims about a draft agreement involving Iran and Oman managing strait traffic a "complete fabrication."

One major unresolved issue in negotiations is whether a U.S.-Iran ceasefire will extend to Israeli operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran has insisted that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement with the United States. Meanwhile, Israeli forces have intensified operations in Lebanon, striking over 550 targets since the beginning of the week and pushing farther north against Hezbollah fighters.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said his military is "deepening its operation" in Lebanon. The fighting has continued despite the U.S.-brokered ceasefire announced in April, which now appears close to collapse. More than 1.2 million Lebanese have been displaced by Israeli strikes and evacuation orders since March 2, when Hezbollah began firing at Israel in support of Iran. Israeli strikes have killed more than 3,200 people in Lebanon, according to the health ministry.

Oil prices jumped 2 percent following Iran's announcement that it had targeted the American base, reflecting market concerns about potential supply disruptions in a region crucial to global petroleum exports.

cards.headline: Inflation Reaches Highest Level Since 2023 as War Drives Prices Higher
cards.body:
Core inflation climbed to an annual rate of 3.3% in April, matching what economists had predicted and marking the highest reading since May 2023. The Federal Reserve released the data using its preferred inflation gauge.

The spike reflects the impact of the ongoing conflict with Iran, which has disrupted energy markets and driven up commodity prices globally. Energy costs have been particularly affected, with oil supply concerns from the region contributing to the broader price increases.

This marks the first inflation report released under newly appointed Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh. The data underscores that prices remain elevated compared to the Fed's target, as war-related pressures continue to affect the economy.

The April result represents a setback after months of declining inflation. Prices had been falling from their 2023 peak before the conflict began disrupting global supply chains and energy markets. The war has essentially reversed recent progress toward price stability.

Federal Reserve officials have signaled they are prepared to use interest rate increases to combat the escalating price pressures. Raising interest rates typically slows economic activity by making borrowing more expensive for both consumers and businesses, which can help cool inflation.

The conflict has created what economists describe as a price shock. Energy costs have surged particularly sharply, reflecting concerns about oil supply disruptions from the region. This energy-driven inflation has pushed the overall reading to its highest level in nearly three years.

Economists had anticipated the 3.3% reading based on price increases observed throughout April related to the war. The confirmation of sustained inflation adds urgency to the Federal Reserve's decision-making at upcoming policy meetings.

The elevated inflation complicates the central bank's efforts to maintain economic stability while supporting growth. The Fed faces pressure to act decisively without triggering unintended consequences for employment and business investment.

Looking ahead, much depends on how the conflict develops. If the war continues, inflation pressures are likely to remain elevated. However, if supply chain disruptions ease in coming months and energy markets stabilize, inflation could moderate.

Analysts note that even a peace deal may not immediately bring relief to consumers. According to energy market experts, US fuel prices are unlikely to return to prewar levels soon, even if the conflict ends quickly. Gas prices that averaged about three dollars per gallon before the war are expected to remain elevated through 2026.

In the UK, the war's impact is also visible in household energy bills, with typical consumers facing annual increases of 221 pounds under the regulator's new price cap. Supply chain experts have warned that Britain's critical infrastructure remains unprepared for major shocks such as war, adding to broader economic concerns.

cards.headline: Nearly half of U.S. households unable to cover basic necessities in 2024
cards.teaser: A new report found that close to half of American households did not earn enough to pay for essentials last year.
cards.body:
Nearly half of U.S. households failed to earn enough income to cover their necessities in 2024, according to a new report. The findings show how close many American families are to financial instability.

The report documents the financial pressures facing households across the country. The data reveals that a substantial portion of the population struggles to meet basic living expenses despite working.

cards.headline: Israel Conducts Strike in Beirut
cards.teaser: Israel launched what it called a targeted strike in the Lebanese capital, which had largely been spared in recent fighting.
cards.body:
Israel carried out a targeted strike in Beirut, marking a significant escalation. The Lebanese capital had previously been largely spared from attacks despite ongoing tensions between Israel and Hezbollah.

Both sides have accused each other of violating the ceasefire agreement reached last month. The strike on Beirut represents a shift in the conflict, as the capital itself had not been targeted until now.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors have launched a criminal probe into the writer who won civil lawsuits against President Trump.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, focusing on whether she made false statements about funding for her civil lawsuits against President Trump, according to multiple reports.

Carroll previously won civil cases against the former president. The investigation represents a significant escalation in the legal disputes between the accuser and Trump.

cards.headline: Federal judge declines to block Trump voting restrictions
cards.teaser: A federal judge refused to temporarily halt an executive order limiting mail-in voting and creating a federal voter list.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to block President Trump's executive order on voting procedures. The order restricts mail-in voting and establishes a federal voter list.

The judge's decision means the executive order remains in effect as legal challenges continue. Additional rulings from other judges may follow.

cards.headline: Russian Tanker Changes Course, Depriving Cuba of Fuel Shipment
cards.teaser: A Russian tanker that appeared to be heading to Cuba with fuel changed direction, a setback for the island facing a U.S. oil blockade.
cards.body:
A Russian tanker that seemed headed to Cuba with fuel changed its route. The development represents a setback for Cuba, which is suffering under a U.S. oil blockade.

The tanker had appeared to be carrying a lifeline of fuel to the island. Its change in direction leaves Cuba without the expected fuel delivery at a time when the country faces significant energy shortages due to American restrictions on oil shipments.

cards.headline: At Least 16 Students Killed in Kenya School Fire
cards.teaser: Dozens more were injured in a dormitory fire at a Kenyan school, the latest in a series of deadly school fires in the country.
cards.body:
A fire broke out just after midnight at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, killing at least 16 students. The blaze tore through a dormitory at the school, located about 76 miles northwest of Nairobi in Kenya's Rift Valley.

Dozens of students were injured in the fire. The incident is part of a troubling pattern of deadly school fires in Kenya in recent years.

cards.headline: Spanish Prime Minister Faces Calls to Resign After Party Office Searched
cards.teaser: A judge accused Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's party of corruption, prompting police to search party offices.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of Spain faced mounting calls to resign after police searched his party's office. A judge accused his party of corruption, leading to the search.

The pressure on Sánchez has grown following the judge's accusations and the subsequent police action. Opposition figures and critics have called for him to step down in response to the corruption allegations against his party.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Opens Criminal Investigation Into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Justice Department launched a criminal probe into the former columnist who successfully sued President Trump.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the former columnist who won a civil lawsuit against President Trump. According to reports, the inquiry focuses on whether Carroll made false statements regarding the funding she received for her civil case against the president.

The investigation represents a significant escalation in the legal disputes between Trump and his accuser.

cards.headline: Middle East Leaders Question Trump's Abraham Accords Proposal
cards.teaser: President Trump said more countries should recognize Israel as part of a deal to end the Iran war, but analysts see little chance of that happening.
cards.body:
President Trump has proposed expanding the Abraham Accords by requiring additional countries to recognize Israel as part of a deal to end the war with Iran. The Abraham Accords previously normalized relations between Israel and several Arab states.

Middle Eastern officials and observers have expressed skepticism about the proposal's viability. Analysts assess that the likelihood of more countries agreeing to recognize Israel under current circumstances is extremely low, leaving many in the region uncertain about how this approach could realistically resolve the conflict.

cards.headline: Italian Police Seize Assets Linked to Mafia Boss
cards.teaser: Authorities in Italy seized what they described as a vast fortune belonging to a legendary Mafia boss.
cards.body:
Police in Italy seized assets they described as a vast fortune belonging to a legendary Mafia boss. The operation targeted wealth accumulated by one of the country's most notorious organized crime figures.

Italian authorities have conducted numerous operations against Mafia-linked assets in recent years. The latest seizure represents another effort to dismantle the financial networks that support organized crime in the country.

cards.body:
Israel struck Beirut in what officials described as a targeted operation. The strike marked a significant escalation for the Lebanese capital, which had previously been largely untouched despite the broader conflict affecting other areas of the country.

The attack came as Israel and Hezbollah continued to accuse each other of violating the ceasefire agreement that began last month. The escalation underscores ongoing tensions between the two sides since the truce took effect.

cards.headline: Nearly half of U.S. households unable to cover basic necessities in 2024
cards.teaser: A new report found that close to half of American households did not earn enough to pay for essentials last year.
cards.body:
Nearly half of U.S. households failed to earn enough income to cover their necessities in 2024, according to a new report. The findings show how close many American families are to financial instability.

The report documents the financial pressures facing households across the country. The data reveals that a substantial portion of the population struggles to meet basic living expenses despite working.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over Polymarket trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a Google staffer with using insider information to make trades on the prediction market platform.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Google software engineer, with using insider information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. According to the complaint, Spagnuolo exploited access to Google's search data to make profitable trades, earning approximately $1.2 million in profits.

Spagnuolo allegedly wagered on long-shot candidates and events that appeared on Google's most-searched list, including indie pop musician D4vd after his arrest made him a trending search topic. The case marks the government's effort to enforce insider trading laws in emerging prediction markets.

cards.headline: Two boys die in heatwave drownings
cards.teaser: A boy was recovered from a pond in Kent and a teenager died in the River Thames during the current heatwave.
cards.body:
Two more boys have died in water-related deaths during the ongoing heatwave. One boy was recovered from a pond in Kent, while another teenager died in the River Thames in Oxford.

The deaths add to a series of water-related fatalities during the period of high temperatures. Authorities have warned about the dangers of swimming in open water during hot weather as people seek relief from the heat.

cards.headline: Australia Sues 3M for $1.4 Billion Over Forever Chemicals
cards.teaser: The lawsuit is the largest ever filed by the Australian government and claims the company concealed information about harmful effects of PFAS.
cards.body:
Australia has filed a A$2 billion lawsuit against 3M, the largest case ever brought by the Australian government. The suit focuses on contamination at defence sites caused by PFAS chemicals, commonly known as forever chemicals, which were used in firefighting foam.

The case alleges that 3M concealed information about the harmful effects of these chemicals. PFAS persist in the environment and human body, and their presence at Australian military installations has prompted the legal action.

cards.headline: Fired BP Chair Rejects Claims About His Dismissal
cards.teaser: Albert Manifold, abruptly removed from the oil company this week, issued a statement defending his conduct.
cards.body:
Albert Manifold, dismissed as BP chair this week, defended his conduct in a statement disputing reports about his behavior. He claimed that during his tenure, no one raised concerns about his conduct or relationships with colleagues.

Manifold rejected characterizations of his dismissal as lies, insisting he always tried to set an example. He also argued that those commenting on his time at BP should not be "allowed to hide behind anonymity."

cards.headline: EU Fines Temu $232 Million for Selling Illegal Products
cards.teaser: The Chinese online retailer was penalized for failing to prevent the sale of illegal and dangerous items on its platform.
cards.body:
The European Commission has imposed a €200 million ($232 million) penalty on Temu for failing to prevent illegal and dangerous products from being sold on its platform. Following a 19-month investigation, regulators found that consumers were very likely to encounter unsafe items, including defective baby toys and faulty chargers.

The fine enforces EU marketplace regulations requiring platforms to take responsibility for the safety of goods sold through their sites. The Commission determined that Temu did not adequately account for the risks posed by these prohibited and unsafe products available to shoppers.

cards.headline: Google Employee Charged With Insider Trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal charges against a Google worker who bet on the prediction market have raised concerns about the growing sector.
cards.body:
A Google software engineer has been charged with insider trading after using confidential information to place bets on Polymarket. Michele Spagnuolo, 36, allegedly leveraged access to Google's search data to wager on outcomes related to the company's Year in Search rankings, generating $1.2 million in profits.

According to the DOJ complaint, Spagnuolo risked over $2.7 million on bets tied to searches that would appear on Google's most-searched list. He reportedly wagered on long-shot candidates, including indie pop musician D4vd, after obtaining non-public information about their search rankings. The case underscores regulatory risks facing prediction markets as they attract participants with access to sensitive data.

cards.headline: Caesars Entertainment Sold for $6 Billion
cards.teaser: The Las Vegas Strip casino operator has been acquired in a major deal.
cards.body:
Caesars Entertainment, a Las Vegas Strip icon, has been sold for $6 billion. The transaction marks a significant deal in the gaming and hospitality industry.

The company operates multiple casino resorts on the Las Vegas Strip and is among the most recognizable names in the casino business.

cards.headline: UK Faces $125 Billion Cost From Young People Not Working or Training
cards.teaser: A new report warns the number of 16 to 24-year-olds out of work, education, or training could reach 1.25 million by 2031.
cards.body:
A new report warns that the UK risks creating a "lost generation" as increasing numbers of young people remain outside the workforce and education system. The number of 16 to 24-year-olds not in work, education, or training is projected to reach 1.25 million by 2031.

The analysis describes the current situation as a "perfect storm" facing British youth, with the economic consequences significant—young people out of work or training are costing the UK £125 billion.

hero.headline: Valve raises Steam Deck prices by more than 40 percent
hero.body:
Valve has increased prices for its Steam Deck handheld gaming device by more than 40 percent, with the company attributing the hikes to the current state of component costs. The price adjustments represent increases of up to $300 depending on the model.

The gaming giant emphasized that the handheld device itself has not changed, only the pricing structure reflects higher manufacturing expenses. The company did not specify which particular components drove the cost increases or provide details about whether the pricing changes are temporary.

The Steam Deck had been out of stock for months before returning to availability at the new higher prices. The device, which launched in 2022, allows users to play PC games on a portable handheld system running a Linux-based operating system with access to games from the Steam digital distribution platform.

Valve offers multiple versions of the hardware at different price points based on storage capacity and screen type. The price increases apply to units currently available for purchase. However, customers who ordered devices before the price changes will receive their units at the previously advertised prices.

The move comes as handheld gaming devices face mounting pressure from supply chain economics. The Steam Deck competes in a growing market of portable gaming systems that includes offerings from manufacturers such as Asus and Lenovo.

Valve has not announced plans to release a new version of the hardware that might offset the higher costs through updated components or manufacturing processes. The company also provided no timeline for how long the increased prices would remain in effect or whether future changes in component costs might allow for price reductions.

The Steam Deck remains available through Valve's official channels at the new pricing. The company has not issued further statements explaining which specific cost pressures necessitated the substantial price increases or provided consumers with clarity about the potential duration of these changes.

The price hikes represent a significant shift for the handheld device, which had established itself in the portable gaming market since its launch three years ago. Industry observers continue to monitor whether other handheld gaming manufacturers will follow suit with their own price adjustments.

cards.headline: Oura launches Ring 5 with 40 percent smaller design and blood pressure detection
cards.teaser: The fifth generation Oura Ring reduces size by 40 percent while adding new health monitoring capabilities.
cards.body:
Oura has launched the Ring 5, its smallest smart ring to date, which is 40 percent smaller and lighter than the Ring 4. The device starts at $399 and features enhanced sensors for more accurate health tracking, along with improved battery life. At just 2.28mm thick, the ring delivers smartwatch-level health monitoring in a more discreet form factor.

The Ring 5 focuses on tracking sleep, stress, readiness, and heart health. The Finnish-American company, valued at $11 billion and backed by 5.5 million users worldwide since its 2013 founding, is preparing for an IPO later this year as it continues expanding its wearables portfolio.

cards.headline: Apple previews iOS 27 with redesigned Siri interface
cards.teaser: New images show Apple's planned overhaul of Siri and AI features in its upcoming iOS 27 operating system.
cards.body:
Apple previewed its iOS 27 operating system with images showing a redesigned Siri interface. The update includes a new Siri app and a feature called Search or Ask that combines search and voice assistant functions.

The operating system update also includes changes to the AirPods settings menu and new controls for Apple's wireless earbuds. The leaked screenshots show Apple's continued push to integrate AI capabilities more deeply into its mobile operating system. iOS 27 is expected to release later this year alongside new iPhone models.

cards.headline: Vertu launches $6,880 AI-powered foldable phone targeting executives
cards.teaser: Luxury phone maker Vertu released a foldable device with integrated AI agent capabilities and enterprise software connections.
cards.body:
Vertu has launched a foldable smartphone starting at $6,880 designed for executives. The device runs on the open-source Hermes project and combines AI-agent workflows with enterprise software integrations.

The phone pairs ultra-premium materials and finishes with AI capabilities positioned as a mobile command center for business management. Vertu has built the device to help CEOs manage company operations from their mobile device.

cards.headline: Forecasters predict below-average Atlantic hurricane season
cards.teaser: Expected El Niño conditions should reduce hurricane activity in the Atlantic this year, though forecasters urge preparedness.
cards.body:
Weather forecasters predict a below-average hurricane season for the Atlantic basin due to anticipated El Niño conditions. The climate pattern typically suppresses hurricane formation in the Atlantic Ocean by increasing wind shear and creating less favorable atmospheric conditions for storm development.

Despite the forecast for fewer storms, meteorologists emphasized that residents in hurricane-prone areas should maintain normal preparedness measures. Even below-average seasons can produce destructive hurricanes, and it only takes one storm making landfall to cause significant damage. Forecasters will continue monitoring conditions throughout the season.

cards.headline: Researchers identify toothless, two-legged crocodile relative from 212 million years ago
cards.teaser: A newly identified species from New Mexico shows ancient crocodile relatives had beaks and walked upright.
cards.body:
Scientists identified a new species of ancient reptile from New Mexico that lived 212 million years ago during the Triassic period. The creature was a bipedal, toothless relative of modern crocodiles that had a beak instead of teeth.

The discovery provides insight into the diversity of crocodile ancestors before dinosaurs became the dominant land animals. The reptile's unusual features, including its upright posture and beak, show that early crocodile relatives occupied different ecological niches than their modern descendants. The species represents a previously unknown branch of the crocodilian family tree.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US manufacturer over chemical contamination at defense sites.
cards.body:
Australia filed a A$2 billion lawsuit against 3M over contamination from forever chemicals in firefighting foam used at defense sites. This represents the largest legal action ever brought by the Australian government.

The case centers on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as PFAS, which were used in firefighting foam at military installations. These chemicals persist in the environment and have raised health concerns globally.

hero.headline: Arsenal faces PSG in Champions League final
hero.body:
Arsenal will play Paris St-Germain in the Champions League final, with the match representing the English club's attempt to win European football's top prize.

PSG could hold an advantage over Arsenal according to analysis of the matchup. The French side's devastating wing play presents a significant tactical challenge for Arsenal.

Full-backs and midfield balance will be key factors in Arsenal's efforts to contain PSG's attacking threats from wide areas. The tactical battle in these areas of the pitch is expected to determine the outcome of the final.

Gabriel Martinelli features prominently in Arsenal's preparations for the final. Arsenal stands one win away from making history by claiming the Champions League trophy.

The final brings together two of Europe's elite clubs in a contest that will decide the continental champion. PSG enters the match with their own ambitions of European glory, having built a squad designed to compete at the highest level.

For Arsenal, victory would represent a historic achievement and the culmination of their season-long European campaign. The club has navigated through the tournament's knockout stages to reach this point.

The tactical setup will focus heavily on how Arsenal manages PSG's wide attackers while maintaining their own offensive threat. Both teams have demonstrated quality throughout the competition to earn their place in the final.

The match represents the final hurdle for Arsenal in their pursuit of Champions League success. PSG will look to use their strengths on the flanks to break down Arsenal's defensive structure and claim the trophy for themselves.

cards.headline: Serena Williams in talks to return at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Serena Williams is considering a return to competitive tennis at Queen's Club next month.
cards.body:
Serena Williams is in discussions about making a competitive return at Queen's Club next month. The prestigious grass-court tournament serves as a traditional warm-up event ahead of Wimbledon on the professional tennis calendar.

A appearance at Queen's would represent Williams' return to competitive play after time away from the sport.

cards.headline: Cristopher Sánchez sets Phillies scoreless innings record
cards.teaser: Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez extended his scoreless streak to 44 innings, breaking a franchise record that stood for 115 years.
cards.body:
Cristopher Sánchez broke a 115-year-old Phillies record by extending his scoreless innings streak to 44. The previous record dated back to 1911, making it one of the franchise's longest-standing marks.

Sánchez made history during a game against the Padres that completed a sweep for Philadelphia. His performance in May has been particularly strong, with the record-setting streak representing the centerpiece of an impressive month on the mound.

cards.headline: Barcelona signs Anthony Gordon from Newcastle
cards.teaser: Barcelona has completed the signing of England international Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.
cards.body:
Barcelona have completed the signing of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle for £69.3m. The England winger underwent a medical on Thursday after the two clubs agreed terms on Wednesday night.

Gordon will double his wages to around £300,000 per week at Camp Nou. Bayern Munich had been frontrunners for the winger's signature, but Gordon's preference for Barcelona allowed the Spanish side to secure the deal ahead of other interested clubs including Liverpool.

cards.headline: Eagles and Patriots trade talks for A.J. Brown continue
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia Eagles and New England Patriots are discussing a trade involving wide receiver A.J. Brown.
cards.body:
The Eagles and Patriots are not particularly close on a potential trade for wide receiver A.J. Brown. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team wants to strengthen the roster wherever possible, including at wide receiver.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts described his relationship with Brown as really good despite the trade speculation. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has weighed in on the possibility of adding Brown to New England's offense.

cards.headline: Rico Verhoeven demands Usyk rematch after stoppage
cards.teaser: Rico Verhoeven is seeking a rematch with Oleksandr Usyk and an apology following a disputed stoppage.
cards.body:
Rico Verhoeven is demanding a rematch with heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk following Saturday's controversial stoppage. The Dutch fighter has also called for an apology from officials over how the bout was concluded.

Verhoeven, who refers to himself as the 'Uncrowned King', believes the stoppage decision was premature. The disputed ending has sparked significant debate about whether the referee should have allowed the fight to continue.

cards.headline: Steve Clarke extends Scotland contract through 2030 World Cup
cards.teaser: Scotland head coach Steve Clarke signed a new contract covering the next two World Cups and the 2028 European Championship.
cards.body:
Scotland manager Steve Clarke has signed a four-year contract extension keeping him in place through the 2030 World Cup and 2028 European Championship. The deal represents a significant commitment from the Scottish Football Association, as Clarke will have managed the national team for 11 years if he sees out the full term, making him Scotland's longest-serving men's manager.

Clarke, 62, initially indicated he would step down after this summer's World Cup, Scotland's first since 1998. However, he subsequently changed course and decided to remain in post. During his tenure since 2019, Clarke has guided Scotland to three of four possible major tournaments.

hero.headline: CNN Sues AI Company Perplexity Over Copyright Infringement
hero.body:
CNN filed a lawsuit against artificial intelligence company Perplexity, accusing the firm of widespread copyright and trademark violations. The suit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The news network alleges Perplexity scraped more than 17,000 CNN stories, photographs, videos and other content without authorization. CNN claims the AI company copied and distributed its material without consent.

The lawsuit centers on allegations that Perplexity used CNN's copyrighted content to build and operate its services. CNN says the company violated intellectual property protections by reproducing and disseminating the network's journalism and branded materials.

The case adds to growing legal battles between traditional media companies and AI firms over the use of copyrighted content. News organizations have increasingly challenged tech companies that use their reporting to train AI systems or generate responses without licensing agreements.

Perplexity operates an AI-powered search and answer engine that provides information to users. The service competes with traditional search engines by generating direct answers to queries rather than simply listing links to source material.

CNN's complaint accuses Perplexity of trademark infringement in addition to copyright violations. The suit suggests the AI company used CNN's brand identity and reputation without permission while distributing the network's content.

The lawsuit seeks to stop Perplexity from continuing to use CNN's material and demands compensation for the alleged infringement. The case represents one of the most significant legal challenges yet from a major news organization against an AI company over content usage.

Neither CNN nor Perplexity immediately provided details about the specific content at issue or the damages being sought. The court filing marks an escalation in tensions between legacy media outlets and emerging AI platforms over how journalistic content can be used in the development and operation of artificial intelligence services.

cards.headline: White House to Host UFC Event for America's 250th Anniversary
cards.teaser: President Trump invited UFC president Dana White to stage a mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary and the president's 80th birthday.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has invited UFC president Dana White to organize a mixed martial arts event on the White House South Lawn. The celebration will mark two significant occasions: the United States' 250th anniversary and Trump's 80th birthday.

The event represents an unprecedented use of the executive mansion's grounds for professional fighting, combining national commemoration with the presidential milestone.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen and Foo Fighters to Headline Tom Morello Festival
cards.teaser: Rage Against the Machine co-founder Tom Morello announced a festival featuring Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters and Dave Matthews Band at Merriweather Post Pavilion near Washington.
cards.body:
Tom Morello organized the Power to the People festival for October 3, 2026 at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland. The Rage Against the Machine co-founder described the event as a celebration of peace, justice, solidarity, music and community action.

Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters and Dave Matthews Band will perform at the concert venue located near Washington. Morello, known for his activism alongside his music career, framed the festival as nonpartisan while emphasizing its focus on community engagement.

cards.headline: Imax Explores Sale Despite Strong Theater Performance
cards.teaser: Imax has attracted moviegoers seeking premium experiences as overall theater attendance has declined in the years following the pandemic.
cards.body:
Imax holds a strong position in the theatrical market as audiences increasingly choose premium viewing options over standard screenings. Movie theater attendance has remained lower than pre-pandemic levels, but customers who do visit cinemas have gravitated toward Imax to differentiate the big screen experience from home viewing.

Despite this favorable market position, the company is for sale. The premium large-format theater brand has benefited from the broader trend of moviegoers willing to pay more for enhanced theatrical experiences when they choose to leave home for entertainment.

cards.headline: SNL U.K. Comedian Ania Magliano Gains Attention for Weekend Update Role
cards.teaser: British comedian Ania Magliano became a standout performer on Saturday Night Live U.K., hosting Weekend Update and taking on controversial topics in the show's premiere.
cards.body:
Ania Magliano, 28, has emerged as a breakout star of "Saturday Night Live U.K." since the show's March premiere. The British comedian made an immediate impact hosting the Weekend Update segment, where she demonstrated a willingness to tackle edgy material.

Magliano cited Tina Fey as a major influence on her comedic approach, aspiring to emulate the veteran's fearless style. She opened the premiere episode with bold commentary, establishing herself as a comedian unafraid of risky jokes that push boundaries.

cards.headline: Influencer Olivia Ponton Renames and Expands Book Podcast
cards.teaser: Model and influencer Olivia Ponton is rebranding her book podcast to include interviews with friends, fans and celebrities alongside authors.
cards.body:
Olivia Ponton announced a new direction for her podcast, renaming it from Booked Busy as she expands its scope. The model and influencer plans to feature conversations with friends, fans and celebrities in addition to author interviews.

Ponton said she aims to challenge stereotypes about people interested in fashion and beauty, showing that intellectual curiosity can coexist with those interests. She described the relaunch as entering a new era for the show.

cards.headline: Disney and Sony Executives Join Paley Center Board
cards.teaser: Walt Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro and Sony president Hiroki Totoki are among entertainment executives joining the Paley Center for Media's board of trustees.
cards.body:
The Paley Center for Media has expanded its board of trustees with three major entertainment industry leaders. Walt Disney Co. CEO Josh D'Amaro, Sony Group Corp. President and CEO Hiroki Totoki, and Liberty Media President and CEO Derek Chang have joined the national board.

Brian Grazer, co-founder and chairman of Imagine Entertainment, was appointed to the Paley Center's Los Angeles Board of Governors.

hero.headline: Federal judge allows Trump mail-in ballot executive order to stand
hero.teaser: A federal judge rejected Democratic legal challenges to President Trump's executive order establishing new rules for mail-in voting.
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. declined to block President Trump's executive order on mail-in voting this week, allowing the directive to proceed despite legal challenges from Democrats. The ruling came after the judge rejected a request for a temporary restraining order.

Trump's March executive order directs the federal government to establish a voter eligibility list using available citizenship data and instructs the US Postal Service to implement new procedures for mail-in ballots. Other judges may still rule on the order's legality.

cards.headline: Former CIA official charged with stealing gold bars worth over $40 million
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors arrested a former CIA official last week for allegedly stealing hundreds of gold bars from the government.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former CIA official who held top secret-level clearance, was charged with criminal theft of public money and arrested last week. Federal officials searched his home earlier this month.

Prosecutors allege Rush stole hundreds of gold bars from the federal government with a total value exceeding $40 million. The charges did not specify when the alleged theft occurred or how Rush gained access to the gold.

cards.teaser: The DNC used profanity in responding to Stephen Miller after he criticized a Texas Senate candidate.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Texas Democratic Senate candidate raises $3 million in 24 hours after GOP runoff
cards.teaser: James Talarico's campaign reported record fundraising after Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in the Republican runoff.
cards.body:
Texas Senate Democratic candidate James Talarico said his campaign raised over $3 million in the 24 hours following Tuesday's Republican runoff election. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won that runoff against Senator John Cornyn.

Talarico described the fundraising as shattering grassroots records. The candidate said contributions came from working people across Texas. The large haul suggests heightened Democratic interest in the race following Paxton's victory in the GOP primary.

cards.headline: Senator Murphy criticizes bipartisan college sports legislation
cards.teaser: Senator Chris Murphy said a new bill regulating college sports would primarily limit athlete compensation.
cards.body:
Senator Chris Murphy cast doubt on new legislation introduced by lawmakers to regulate college sports. The Connecticut Democrat wrote in a social media post Wednesday night that the bill's primary effect appears to limit athlete compensation.

The legislation was described as bipartisan and aims to address the business of college sports. Murphy's criticism suggests Democratic opposition to at least some provisions of the bill, though he did not detail specific objections beyond athlete pay concerns.

cards.headline: Beto O'Rourke calls James Talarico best candidate he has seen in Texas politics
cards.teaser: The former congressman praised the Texas state representative during an interview on MSNBC.
cards.body:
Former Representative Beto O'Rourke said state Representative James Talarico is the best candidate he has seen during his time in Texas politics. O'Rourke made the comments during an interview with host Jen Psaki on MSNBC.

O'Rourke described Talarico as the best over the course of his life running and being involved in politics in Texas. The endorsement from O'Rourke, who ran for Senate and governor in recent years, provides a boost to Talarico's Senate campaign.

cards.headline: White House posts Harambe tribute on social media
cards.teaser: The White House marked what would have been the 27th birthday of the gorilla who died in 2016.
cards.body:
The White House paid tribute to Harambe, the gorilla whose 2016 death became an internet meme. On what would have been his 27th birthday, the official White House account posted on social media calling him "a true patriot" and marking the occasion with the message "Forever in our hearts."

Harambe was shot and killed at the Cincinnati Zoo after a toddler entered his enclosure and interacted with the 400-pound western lowland gorilla. The incident sparked widespread online mourning and made the animal a lasting cultural phenomenon.
